paper_type_evidence.quote: We searched for CO$^+$ absorption with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) towards two quasars with known Galactic foreground absorption from diffuse interstellar gas

evidence.quote: The targeted sources are J1717-3342 and J1744-3116, two bright quasars situated at small galactic latitude behind the Galactic bulge

question.value: Is thermal cosmic-ray and UV-driven chemistry producing CO in diffuse interstellar molecular gas through the intermediate formation of CO+?

evidence.quote: To test whether the thermal cosmic-ray and UV-driven chemistry is producing CO in diffuse interstellar molecular gas through the intermediate formation of CO$^+$.

claims.hypothesis: CO+ is abundant enough in diffuse molecular gas to be an intermediate on the path to HCO+ and CO
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 search for CO+ N=2-1 absorption toward two quasars behind diffuse Galactic gas
claims.result: No CO+ detected; N(CO+)/N(HCO+) < ~0.04 and X(CO+) < 1.2e-10
claims.finding: CO+ is too scarce to be the main precursor of HCO+ in diffuse gas

evidence.quote: We could not detect CO$^+$ but obtained sensitive upper limits toward both targets.

claims.hypothesis: CO+ + H2 -> HCO+ + H can replenish the HCO+ lost to recombination
claims.experiment: Steady-state balance of HCO+ formation via CO+ + H2 against recombination, compared with the upper limits
claims.result: Required CO+/HCO+ is some 25 times above the limit and required X(CO+) at least 15 times above it
claims.finding: CO+ produces at most a few percent of the HCO+ that recombines to form CO

evidence.loc: 3.2 CO+ as a source of HCO+
evidence.quote: CO$^+$ is responsible for producing at most a few percent of the HCO$^+$ that recombines with ambient thermal electrons to form CO in diffuse molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: A thermal cosmic-ray and UV-driven chemistry can reproduce the observed CO+, HOC+ and HCO+ abundances
claims.experiment: Equilibrium gas-sphere chemical model with variations of key rates and abundances
claims.result: Baseline model gives CO+ below the limits but overproduces HOC+ by about a factor two (up to six with fast isomerization)
claims.finding: Fit is better if C+ + H2O preferentially forms HCO+; some aspects of the C+ + H2O reaction may be not fully understood

evidence.quote: A baseline cosmic-ray and UV-driven thermal chemical model overproduced HOC$^+$ by a factor two, but by as much as a factor six

claims.hypothesis: Modest densities suffice for CO formation through HCO+ recombination in diffuse gas
claims.experiment: n(H)/G0 derived from N(CO)/N(HCO+) for a sample of QSO sight lines as function of E(B-V)
claims.result: Mean n(H)/G0 ~300 cm^-3; n(H) ~100-300 cm^-3 for E(B-V) >~ 0.5 mag but ~1-2e3 cm^-3 at E(B-V) ~0.1-0.2 mag
claims.finding: Modest densities suffice at high extinction; low-extinction CO requires over-pressured gas (turbulent dissipation chemistry) or a lower radiation field

evidence.quote: such heavily over-pressured gas is more properly considered in the context of a turbulent dissipation chemistry

why_this_data.value: N=2-1 near 236 GHz chosen because it is accessible from the ground and remains populated in diffuse gas; targets are bright quasars with known high Galactic foreground molecular columns

evidence.quote: We chose to search for the $N=2\rightarrow1$ transitions because the frequencies of this first excited transition near 236 GHz are easily accessible from ground-based radio observatories
that were known to have high intervening column densities of Galactic neutral gas detected in molecular absorption

why_this_method.value: Absorption spectroscopy is the best probe of diffuse-cloud molecular content because excitation is weak and levels are in the lowest rotational states

evidence.quote: Absorption spectroscopy represents the best method to probe the molecular content of diffuse clouds because the molecular excitation is weak at the low densities

evidence.quote: The CO$^+$ ground state rotational transitions at 117.7 GHz and 118.1 GHz are close to a strong atmospheric line from molecular oxygen at 118.75 GHz, rendering their observation from the ground very difficult.

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits depend on the assumed CMB-only excitation (2.73 K) and on the adopted HCO+ abundance of 3e-9 for N(H2)
Chemical model is described only in outline; no code, grid or parameter table is provided to rerun Fig. 3
Spectra taken only at the continuum peak from pipeline products; no quoted checks on calibration, flux scale or continuum subtraction
Table 3 prints J1744-3416 for the second source, an apparent typo for J1744-3116

missing_for_reproduction: Calibration and extraction details (continuum level, line-free channels, rms and upper-limit computation)
Observing log (dates, configuration, time on source, calibrators other than the bandpass calibrator)
Chemical model code and full parameter set for Fig. 3 and Fig. 4
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: two targets, Band 6, one tuning with a few spectral windows (likely a few GB to tens of GB of raw data)
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code and final numeric tables are given and the spectral extraction is simple, but pipeline version, calibrators, extraction/limit procedure and the chemical model code are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The observational part (CO+ non-detection limits and column densities) is numeric and rests on a single archive-linked project with simple extraction, although public status is not stated in the paper and the chemical modelling is not reproducible from the text.
